focus: Original proposals Ponytail inspires but does not contain, plus the consolidated rejection set
noveltyJustification: Eight original proposals, each grounded in an artifact read in iterations 1-8 and each stating why Ponytail cannot contain it (doctrine-effect scenarios, two-layer scenario verdicts, grader self-test precondition, restraint-counterweight pairing rule, retirement-note contract, external-anchor requirement, reuse-evidence rung, anti-fabricated-baseline rule); the rejection consolidation adds no new facts.
keyQuestions: Which Ponytail ideas should be rejected for sk-code and why, and what original ideas does Ponytail inspire that it does not contain?
answeredQuestions: Which Ponytail ideas should be rejected for sk-code and why, and what original ideas does Ponytail inspire that it does not contain?
ruledOut: Presenting any proposal as a copy of a Ponytail artifact
Proposing a new tool, dependency or framework (every proposal attaches to an existing surface)

graphEvents.label: Reuse-evidence rung shared with removal proposals
Ponytail and hub artifacts read in iterations 1-8

label: ORIGINAL: doctrine-effect scenarios probing whether the hub's own load-bearing rules (SCOPE-LOCK, durable-WHY comment hygiene, ladder reuse rung, no-verdict envelope vocabulary) change model output, with a control arm; inspired by behavior.yaml, impossible in Ponytail because it has no scope-lock, routing or envelope. Classification: NEW/ORIGINAL.

ORIGINAL: two-layer scenario verdicts making a deterministic routing precondition and a separate behavior verdict first-class, so the existing 28-scenario corpus regains an offline CI gate while the live behavior claim stays legible; inspired by the retired benchmark report's own note, impossible in Ponytail because it has no routing layer. Classification: NEW/ORIGINAL.

ORIGINAL: a grader self-test precondition requiring scenario detection markers to be machine-checkable and each checker to carry a negative fixture it must reject, so a PASS is not purely a judgment call; inspired by Ponytail's API-key-free grader test, impossible in Ponytail because it has no scenario corpus or detection markers. Classification: NEW/ORIGINAL.

ORIGINAL: a restraint-counterweight pairing rule stating that a restraint metric may not be published alone but ships with a correctness counterweight and, where warranted, an adversarial tier in the same artifact; specifies what the prior supporting-evidence allowance pairs with, and governs the pending Lane B code_loc metric. Classification: NEW/ORIGINAL.

ORIGINAL: a retirement-note contract requiring a retired guard's umbrella to name the successor guard or record the coverage gap with a named owner; the hub's drift-guard note records the retired router-sync check as missing with neither, and the gap is acknowledged in two places. Classification: NEW/ORIGINAL.

ORIGINAL: an external-anchor requirement for agreement guards, so any guard proving two artifacts agree names the truth source outside the pair; the hub's agent-mirror gate already satisfies it, and the requirement protects the next agreement guard from being written without one. Classification: NEW/ORIGINAL.

ORIGINAL: a reuse-evidence rung on the restraint ladder requiring either a citation of the reused existing export or an explicit statement that the search found none, with removal proposals citing the same inventory to show no consumer exists; fuses Ponytail's codebase-map mechanism, the ladder and the removal-plan evidence field into one citable rule. Classification: NEW/ORIGINAL.

ORIGINAL: an anti-fabricated-baseline rule for research and refinement packets stating that a claimed size, cost or time reduction is not reportable unless a paired measurement ran; derived from Ponytail's refusal to print per-repo savings numbers, and self-applying to this packet's own phases. Classification: NEW/ORIGINAL.
